title: Tamago Kake Gohan
subtitle: raw egg over hot rice
excerpt: Tamago kake gohan is hot steamed rice with a raw egg cracked directly over it, seasoned with soy sauce. The heat of the rice partially cooks the egg to create a creamy, rich coating. Serves 1 to 4.
sourceNotes: Tamago kake gohan has been eaten in Japan since at least the Meiji era. It is considered a quintessential Japanese breakfast. The dish requires very fresh eggs and good-quality soy sauce. In Japan it is abbreviated to TKG and has a devoted following.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Japanese breakfast dish of hot steamed rice topped with a raw egg and soy sauce. The egg is stirred in and the heat of the rice gently cooks it to a soft, creamy consistency.
The Japanese word for soy sauce. In tamago kake gohan, high-quality shoyu is essential as it is the only seasoning in the dish.

content.text: depends on two things: very hot freshly cooked rice and a very fresh egg. The rice must be just cooked and steaming hot when the egg goes on. Good
Use the freshest eggs you can find, ideally from a producer you trust. The egg is not fully cooked so its quality matters more here than in any other recipe.

items.prepNote: optional, a small drizzle per bowl
cut into thin strips, to garnish

content.text: Cook the short-grain rice by the absorption method. Bring to the boil, reduce to the lowest heat, cover and cook for 12 minutes. Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 more minutes.
Scoop the hot rice into individual bowls immediately. The rice must be as hot as possible.
Crack one egg over each bowl of rice. Drizzle about half a tablespoon of soy sauce over the egg.
Stir vigorously with chopsticks to break the egg and mix it through the rice. The heat of the rice will partially cook the egg, making it creamy and thick.
Add a small drizzle of sesame oil if using. Top with nori strips, spring onion and sesame seeds. Eat immediately while the rice is hot.

attrs.symptom: Egg remains completely raw and liquid
attrs.cause: Rice was not hot enough when the egg was added
attrs.fix: The rice must be freshly cooked and steaming. Leftover or cooled rice will not raise the egg temperature enough.

attrs.cause: Not enough soy sauce or a low-quality soy sauce was used
attrs.fix: Use a good-quality Japanese soy sauce. Taste after stirring and add a few more drops. The seasoning must be balanced.

attrs.symptom: Rice and egg do not combine smoothly
attrs.fix: Stir very briskly for 20 to 30 seconds. The friction and heat need to be worked through the rice to emulsify the egg.

content.text: Tamago kake gohan is the simplest of Japanese breakfast foods. It is eaten across Japan every morning, often with a bowl of miso soup alongside. In Japan, people have strong opinions about their preferred brand of soy sauce for TKG. Some chefs separate the yolk from the white, using only the yolk for a richer result. The dish takes under a minute to assemble once the rice is ready.
